title: Isolated recovery-authorization signer with derived permit semantics

scientific_correspondence.derivation: P16 scientific correspondence established a 1058-test governance baseline. Compare 3727a6cc0972c9995f1b4523b1b9f519ea4ace48...9e409e411c3fd5e4c2a1b9b9ac90d0145f7d6141 shows exactly one new governance test file. Exact frozen P17 source contains P17-01 through P17-16. The unchanged workflow discovers every governance test_*.py and its governor step succeeded.

mechanism_evidence: Recovery authorization signing executes in a distinct subprocess with its own durable issuance ledger and internally derived private-key path.
Caller request surface supplies only recovery identity and target selector; governed permit semantics are derived from authenticated root history and trusted-minimum state.
Recovery private key and direct sign primitive are absent from caller, minimum-authority, root-trust, registry-writer, model, and reviewer surfaces tested by the frozen vectors.
Only the exact contiguous authenticated root immediately above the current trusted minimum is issuable.
Caller-supplied epochs, digests, fingerprints, predecessor values, transition identifiers, activation epochs, and authority claims do not alter the signed permit.
Durable issuance memory provides exact replay identity and same-recovery-ID rebinding refusal across signer restart.
Signer outage produces no new permit and no trusted-minimum mutation.
Concurrent exact issuance requests converge on one permit/signature and one issuance-ledger record.
Minimum-side use-time revalidation catches state drift after permit issuance.
Clean signer-derived R2-to-R3 recovery remains live after R1-to-R2 advancement.
bounded_claim: On the tested same-host process-isolated SQLite/software-key prototype, recovery-authorization issuance was isolated behind a dedicated signer process that derived governed permit semantics from authenticated root history and trusted-minimum state rather than accepting caller-supplied bindings. The frozen tests denied forged, injected, stale, noncontiguous, rebound, unavailable, restarted, raced, and post-issuance-drift scenarios while preserving exact replay and clean R2-to-R3 liveness.
not_proven: OS-user, privilege, or administrative trust-domain separation merely from process isolation.
KMS/HSM key nonextractability or hardware-backed recovery signing.
Protection after joint compromise of recovery signer private material/ledger and minimum-authority state.
Abrupt signer process death at individual issuance transaction boundaries.
Physical power-loss or storage-controller durability semantics.
Production, release, deploy, or completion authority.
next_falsification_target: EXP-I Pilot 18: abrupt external termination around recovery-authorization issuance. Use parent-observed child readiness and external process termination before issuance transaction, after issuance-ledger insert before commit, after durable commit before response, and during replay/rebinding paths. Reopen the signer from a fresh process and falsify false issuance, duplicate permit creation, semantic rebinding, stale issuance, race amplification, and minimum mutation from ambiguous issuance while preserving exact post-commit replay and clean R2-to-R3 liveness.
